answer: A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The violet multiplier is published, charged in sparrow, and glacier lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 5 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 4909 identities would post 3636 proofs and burn roughly 88 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
